To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. LSTM models can generalize to unseen data in a formal language, 2. The model performance depends on the training data regime (i.e., whether training data is generated by a context-free grammar), 3. The model performance also depends on the model capacity (i.e., the number of hidden units)

(i) LSTM networks can learn to generate the target languages with a training set size of only 1000 samples, (ii) LSTM networks are not capable of generalizing to unseen samples if trained on a small training set of 100 samples, (iii) the generalization capabilities of LSTM networks increase when the training set size is increased, and (iv) LSTM networks are able to generalize to unseen samples when the model capacity is increased.2
• The generalization performance of LSTM networks on formal languages is highly sensitive to training regime, model capacity and language size.
